formal_method_source: GAO Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide GAO-20-195G, chapter on parametric estimating; NASA Cost Estimating Handbook version 4.0, cost estimating relationships. The registry label is not a named algorithm: it is a label for parametric cost estimating.
formulation_selected: a cost estimating relationship fitted to a historical population, predicting cost from measured driver quantities, with a stated basis of estimate and an error treatment
alternative_formulations: the functional form is a modelling choice (linear, power, learning curve) and the fitting method is a modelling choice (ordinary least squares, weighted, robust). These are choices within one agreed method, not competing definitions of it.
canonical_problem_description: five historical observations lying exactly on cost = 100 + 5 times quantity; fit by ordinary least squares; predict at a quantity of 60
independent_expected_result: intercept 100, slope 5, prediction 400, residual zero. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: the ratio of a cost-index forecast to a remaining-work forecast, which is an algebraic identity in the two forecasts
defining_components_missing: a cost driver set; a cost estimating relationship; fitted coefficients; units; a historical calibration population; an uncertainty or error treatment; a basis of estimate
missing_data_structure: a cost driver quantity field on the project record, and a stored relationship with its fitted coefficients
missing_reference_data: a historical population of completed projects with driver quantities and final costs, which this platform does not hold
application_mapping_supported: YES, if drivers and a historical population are collected
implementation_effort_summary: substantial: a new data structure, a collection programme for historical projects, a fitting step and an error model. The arithmetic is the smallest part.
owner_decision_required: the disposition of this module, and whether the platform is to collect cost driver quantities at all

formal_method_source: Smarandache, Extension of Soft Set to Hypersoft Set, and then to Plithogenic Hypersoft Set, Neutrosophic Sets and Systems 22 (2018), 168 to 170. The primary PDF host is blocked by this container egress proxy; the definition below is taken from retrievable secondary reproductions that agree with each other.
formulation_selected: a pair (F, A1 x ... x An) over a universe U where the Ai are pairwise disjoint attribute value sets and F maps each tuple of the Cartesian product to a SUBSET of U
alternative_formulations: none material: the definition is stable across the sources reached
canonical_problem_description: universe of four objects; two disjoint attribute value sets of two values each; F given on all four tuples of the product
independent_expected_result: the mapping is total on the product, the attribute value sets are disjoint, and every image is a subset of the universe. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: a scalar score looked up from a table keyed on a genuine three-attribute tuple
defining_components_present: the multi-argument tuple over three attribute value sets; disjoint attribute value sets; a mapping keyed on the product
defining_components_missing: a universe of objects to return a subset of; a total mapping over the product; a set-valued codomain; any source for the twenty-five literal scores
missing_data_structure: a universe of objects, so the mapping can return a subset rather than a number
missing_reference_data: a source for the mapped values
implementation_effort_summary: moderate: the tuple structure is already correct. Completing the mapping over the product is small. Making the codomain a subset of a universe requires deciding what the universe is.
owner_decision_required: what the universe of objects is to be, and where the mapped values come from

formal_method_source: Smarandache, Plithogenic Set, an Extension of Crisp, Fuzzy, Intuitionistic Fuzzy, and Neutrosophic Sets, and Plithogeny, Plithogenic Set, Logic, Probability and Statistics (2017). Primary PDF hosts blocked by the egress proxy; the quintuple and the two contradiction-function properties are corroborated across the retrievable reproductions.
formulation_selected: the quintuple (P, v, Pv, pdf, pCF): an attribute with a value set, a degree of appurtenance function, and a degree of contradiction function defined between each attribute value and a designated DOMINANT value, with pCF(a,a) = 0 and pCF(a,b) = pCF(b,a); aggregation is a contradiction-weighted combination of a t-norm and a t-conorm
alternative_formulations: the exact coefficient convention of the aggregation operator varies between presentations and the primary text could not be reached to fix it. The finding does NOT depend on that choice: the module designates no dominant value at all, so pCF is undefined under every convention.
canonical_problem_description: one attribute with three values, a designated dominant value, and a contradiction function given on the pairs
independent_expected_result: the contradiction degree is zero on the diagonal, symmetric, and taken relative to the designated dominant value. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: a contradiction-weighted aggregate of literal appurtenance degrees attached to status bands
defining_components_present: appurtenance degrees; a contradiction figure; an aggregation that uses both
defining_components_missing: a designated dominant attribute value; a contradiction function of a PAIR of attribute values; measured rather than literal degrees; a defined attribute value set
missing_data_structure: an attribute value set with a designated dominant value, so the contradiction degree has something to be relative to
missing_reference_data: a source for the appurtenance degrees, which are currently three literals
implementation_effort_summary: moderate: the aggregation shape is close. Designating a dominant value and making the contradiction degree a function of a pair is the real work, and it is a modelling decision before it is a coding one.
owner_decision_required: which attribute value is dominant, and where the appurtenance degrees come from

formal_method_source: Busemeyer and Bruza, Quantum Models of Cognition and Decision, Cambridge University Press 2012, chapters 2 and 4; the Born rule as standard quantum probability.
formulation_selected: a normalised state in a Hilbert space, an orthogonal family of projectors summing to the identity, outcome probabilities as squared projection norms, and interference as a cross term between amplitudes
alternative_formulations: state-vector and density-operator presentations are equivalent for this purpose and are not competing definitions
canonical_problem_description: a two-dimensional real normalised state (0.6, 0.8) with projectors onto the two basis rays
independent_expected_result: Born probabilities 0.36 and 0.64, summing to exactly one. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: square roots of averaged literal classical probabilities, with an interference term scaled by a bare constant and a phase angle that is a tally of adverse indicators
defining_components_missing: a normalised state; a state vector or density operator; projectors; the Born rule; a phase that is continuous in the state
missing_data_structure: a state representation and a projector family
missing_reference_data: none: the method needs no historical population
application_mapping_supported: YES, if what the state and the outcomes are meant to represent is decided
implementation_effort_summary: substantial rewrite. The measured squared amplitudes sum to about 0.86, the phase takes four values, and neither is a small correction. This is weighted scoring wearing the vocabulary of the method.
owner_decision_required: whether a genuine quantum probability model is wanted here at all, and what its state and outcomes would represent

formal_method_source: Ehrgott, Multicriteria Optimization, 2nd edition, Springer 2005; Miettinen, Nonlinear Multiobjective Optimization, Kluwer 1999.
formulation_selected: decision variables over a feasible set, at least two objective functions with stated directions, and a solution concept: a nondominated set, a weighted scalarisation with stated weights, or an epsilon-constraint formulation
alternative_formulations: the three solution concepts named above are genuinely different and the platform has not chosen between them. This is a choice the owner must make, not a gap in the literature.
canonical_problem_description: four candidate alternatives with two objectives, both maximised
independent_expected_result: the nondominated set is A, B and C; D is dominated by B; the answer is invariant under reordering. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: the equally weighted mean of three normalised indicators for one project
defining_components_present: three quantities that could serve as objectives
defining_components_missing: decision variables; a feasible set; candidate alternatives; a stated solution concept; stated weights
missing_data_structure: a set of candidate alternatives with objective vectors, visible to the analytical layer. The platform DOES generate courses of action, but only in the browser at display time from a stored row, so the analytical layer never sees a set.
missing_reference_data: none: the method needs no historical population
application_mapping_supported: YES, and more cheaply than it looks, because a set of alternatives already exists in the product and simply does not reach this layer
implementation_effort_summary: moderate: assemble the courses of action server side as objective vectors, then choose and implement one solution concept.
owner_decision_required: which solution concept is intended, and whether the courses of action are to be assembled server side

formal_method_source: Dantzig, Linear Programming and Extensions, Princeton University Press 1963; Hillier and Lieberman, Introduction to Operations Research, chapter 3.
formulation_selected: maximise or minimise a linear objective subject to linear constraints and bounds, solved to an optimum, with infeasibility and unboundedness determined by the constraint system
alternative_formulations: none: the definition is not in dispute
canonical_problem_description: the Wyndor Glass problem of Hillier and Lieberman: maximise 3x + 5y subject to x at most 4, 2y at most 12, 3x + 2y at most 18, x and y at least zero
independent_expected_result: the published optimum is 36 at x equal to 2 and y equal to 6. Reproduced independently by vertex enumeration in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: the cost index a project would need to finish inside its remaining budget, that is one ratio with a threshold on it
defining_components_missing: decision variables; an objective vector; a constraint matrix; bounds; a solver; any representation of unboundedness
missing_data_structure: a program representation: variables, objective coefficients, a constraint matrix and bounds
missing_reference_data: none: the method needs no historical population
application_mapping_supported: YES, if what is being allocated and under what constraints is decided
implementation_effort_summary: substantial: a program representation and a solver, plus the modelling work of deciding what the decision variables are. A pure-Python simplex for problems of this size is small; the modelling is not.
owner_decision_required: what decision this program is meant to make, and what the variables and constraints are

formal_method_source: Saltelli et al., Global Sensitivity Analysis: The Primer, Wiley 2008, chapter 1, on one-at-a-time designs.
formulation_selected: perturb an input by a stated amount, RECOMPUTE the output or the decision, and report how and by how much it moved, with a zero-perturbation control
alternative_formulations: one-at-a-time, variance-based and derivative-based designs differ, but all of them require a recomputation. The module performs none, so the choice does not affect the finding.
canonical_problem_description: a two-input decision rule; perturb schedule down by a tenth and cost up by a tenth
independent_expected_result: the schedule perturbation flips the decision from proceed to review; the cost perturbation does not; a zero perturbation moves nothing. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: the share of a scaled total distance from fixed reference values carried by each of three inputs
defining_components_present: a driver ranking that does respond when an input actually changes
defining_components_missing: a stated perturbation size; a recomputation of the decision; a before and after comparison; a zero-perturbation control
missing_data_structure: an argument for a perturbation size, and access to the decision computation to re-run it
missing_reference_data: none: the method needs no historical population
application_mapping_supported: YES, and this is the most tractable of the eight: the platform already computes decisions and can be asked to compute them again under a changed input
implementation_effort_summary: small to moderate: call the existing decision computation once per perturbed input and report the difference. The scale factors of one hundred and fifty in the present code would go.
owner_decision_required: which inputs are to be perturbed and by how much, and whether the sensitivity is of the decision or of the score

formal_method_source: Ehrgott, Multicriteria Optimization, 2nd edition, Springer 2005, definition of Pareto optimality and the nondominated set.
formulation_selected: over a set of alternatives with objective vectors, the nondominated subset: those alternatives no other matches on every objective while beating on at least one
alternative_formulations: none: the dominance relation is not in dispute
canonical_problem_description: the same four alternatives with two objectives used for the multi-objective section
independent_expected_result: the frontier is A, B and C; D is dominated; the answer is invariant under reordering. Verified in the harness.
current_code_actual_method: three threshold tests on one project, labelled with the vocabulary of dominance
defining_components_present: nothing: dominance is a relation and the module holds one point
defining_components_missing: a set of alternatives; objective vectors; a pairwise dominance relation; a nondominated set
missing_data_structure: a set of candidate alternatives with objective vectors, visible to the analytical layer. As with the multi-objective module, courses of action exist but only in the browser at display time.
missing_reference_data: none: the method needs no historical population
application_mapping_supported: YES, on the same footing as the multi-objective module
implementation_effort_summary: small once the alternatives exist: the dominance relation is a few lines. Supplying the set is the whole of the work, and it is shared with the multi-objective module.
owner_decision_required: whether the courses of action are to be assembled server side as objective vectors, which would serve this module and the multi-objective one together
